008package paint.viewer.app;
009
010import paint.shared.config.paintconfig.PaintConfig;
011import paint.ui.dialogs.ProjectDialog;
012import paint.ui.dialogs.ProjectDialog.DialogMode;
013import paint.shared.utils.PaintLogger;
014import paint.shared.utils.PaintPrefs;
015import paint.viewer.model.RecordingEntry;
016import paint.viewer.model.RecordingLoader;
017import paint.viewer.ui.frames.ViewerFrame;
018
019import javax.swing.*;
020import java.nio.file.Path;
021import java.util.List;
022
023/**
024 * Main entry point for the PAINT Viewer application.
025 * <p>
026 * This class sets up preferences, configuration, and logging, and then opens
027 * the project selection dialog. Once the user confirms their selection, it
028 * loads the corresponding recordings and launches the main viewer interface.
029 * </p>
030 */
031public class Viewer {
032
033    /**
034     * Application entry point.
035     *
036     * @param args command-line arguments (unused)
037     */
038    public static void main(String[] args) {
039        SwingUtilities.invokeLater(() -> {
040
041            // --- Step 1: Load last-used project from preferences ---
042            String lastProject = PaintPrefs.getString("Path", "Project Root", System.getProperty("user.home"));
043            Path   projectPath = Path.of(lastProject);
044
045            // --- Step 2: Initialise logging and configuration ---
046            PaintConfig.initialise(projectPath);
047            PaintLogger.initialise(projectPath, "Viewer");
048            PaintLogger.setLevel(PaintPrefs.getString("Runtime", "Log Level", "INFO"));
049
050            // --- Step 3: Show the project specification dialog ---
051            ProjectDialog specificationDialog =
052                    new ProjectDialog(null, projectPath, DialogMode.VIEWER);
053
054            // Callback when user presses OK
055            specificationDialog.setCalculationCallback(project -> {
056                try {
057                    List<RecordingEntry> recordingEntries =
058                            RecordingLoader.loadFromProject(project);
059
060                    if (recordingEntries.isEmpty()) {
061                        JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(
062                                null,
063                                "No valid recordings found in selected experiments.",
064                                "No Recordings",
065                                JOptionPane.WARNING_MESSAGE
066                        );
067                        return false;
068                    }
069
070                    ViewerFrame viewer = new ViewerFrame(project, recordingEntries);
071                    viewer.setVisible(true);
072                    return true;
073
074                } catch (Exception ex) {
075                    // Log the cause, not just the fact. This used to discard `ex` entirely, which
076                    // made every startup failure undiagnosable — and it silently hid the case where
077                    // ViewerFrame could not build its grid, leaving the user with nothing at all.
078                    PaintLogger.error("Viewer launch failed", ex);
079                    JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(
080                            null,
081                            "The Viewer could not be opened:\n\n" + ex.getMessage(),
082                            "Viewer failed to start",
083                            JOptionPane.ERROR_MESSAGE
084                    );
085                    return false;
086                }
087            });
088
089            // --- Step 4: Open dialog (blocking) ---
090            specificationDialog.showDialog();
091        });
092    }
093}
